messages:
mira: 🚨 FleetNova is hitting repeated 429 throttles on their Dedicated pool since ~09:12 UTC. Customers report 200–800ms tail latency bursts then a burst of 429s. Opening thread with traces and initial logs.

kai: copying logs. do we have tenant id + pool id? I can start digging into autoscaler events.

mira: tenant=fleetnova-prod-1, pool=d-ed-tn-07, request pattern = short chat completions, high qps bursts at ~100 rps sustained for ~30s windows. last 429 window: 09:11:45–09:13:10. attaching small trace snippet below.

alex: @kai can you pull the autoscaler history for pool d-ed-tn-07 around that time? suspect scale-up latency + cooldown too short.

sre-bot: [alert] d-ed-tn-07 autoscale: scale_down event at 2026-02-18T09:10:50Z -> scale_up at 2026-02-18T09:11:40Z -> 429 spike at 09:11:55Z (post-scale-up). See runbook link: https://intra.redwood/ops/autoscale

kai: got the events. pattern: scale_down -> immediate small burst -> scale_up -> KV cache cold-start -> a flurry of requests overwhelm warmup causing token-level QPS to spike -> internal throttles fire. metrics copied:
- cpu_util pct: 15 -> 80 -> 72
- active_requests: 4 -> 98 -> 85
- queue_depth: 1 -> 40 -> 3

mira: logs show many client retries in small window which amplifies. sample request flow:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-like","inputs":"ping"}'
```
Clients are retrying on timeouts, making burstiness worse.

alex: this looks like a classic scale-jitter where cooldowns are too aggressive and cache warmup is slow. Two immediate mitigations: 1) enable short burst capacity so scale_up can oversubscribe temporarily, 2) increase scale_down cooldown (or add hysteresis) so we avoid downscaling during short troughs.

gina-support: customer-facing update drafted: "We're investigating autoscaling instability on your dedicated pool and will apply mitigations to stabilize throughput. ETA 30m." Want me to send?

mira: yes please send the update. also asking infra to run tenant isolation check - maybe noisy neighbor from another tenant on same node group.

kai: I ran top tenants on node group: fleetnova-prod-1 accounts for 62% mem, 55% peak tokens during the window. There is one other tenant (beta-ops) with large batched embeddings at 09:10 which coincides. noisy neighbor possible.

alex: action plan I propose:
- short term (now): increase scale_down cooldown from 60s -> 180s for pool d-ed-tn-07; enable burst capacity (burst_slots=2) for 1 hour.
- medium term: add KV cache warmup prefetch for pinned model variants on scale_up, and tune autoscaler threshold to consider queue_depth with 30s smoothing.
- long term: tenant isolation option for heavy batch workloads (move beta-ops to a separate pool).

mira: can we apply the short term changes w/o restart? prefer config flip.

kai: yes can flip config via control plane. I will patch policy now and watch. patch id: cp-change-8117. applying.

sre-bot: [deploy] control-plane config cp-change-8117 applied to d-ed-tn-07 at 2026-02-18T09:28:40Z

kai: patched cooldown -> 180s and burst_slots enabled. monitoring window open for 30m. also added smoothing factor to queue_depth aggregation.

mira: thanks. @gina-support please update FleetNova with the change and note we will monitor for 24h and follow up with postmortem if it recurs.

gina-support: sent: "We've enabled temporary autoscale stabilization measures (extended cooldown + burst capacity). We'll monitor and follow up within 24 hours." customer asked about root cause — told them we suspect brief noisy neighbor + cache warmup coupling.

alex: initial telemetry looks better: immediate 429s dropped to single-digit counts in the last 10m, tail latency reduced. still seeing small bumps when large batch jobs hit — need to isolate.

kai: next steps: 1) schedule a tenant migration for beta-ops to a different node group (ops ticket #INC-5942), 2) bake KV-cache prefetch for model variants (RFC-332), 3) add autoscaler unit test for scale_jitter scenario.

mira: assigning tasks: @kai -> apply migration plan and monitor; @alex -> write RFC for prefetch; @gina-support -> coordinate customer comms and confirm after 24h; I will own postmortem if we get recurrence.

gina-support: acknowledged, will ping customer after 24h and update support ticket.

alex: quick note for postmortem: capture request retry behavior + client backoff patterns, we might want to add server-side retry-smoothing header to advise clients.

kai: logging a runbook improvement PR: https://git.internal/redwood/ops/merge/1234 (adds scale-jitter troubleshooting steps).

mira: thanks team. tentatively closing this incident as mitigated; will reopen if 429s reappear. :white_check_mark:
